# Critique — Twenty Ways the First Plan Could Fail

The Awtsmoos tears false certainty from the wall; Awtsmoos.com must survive scale, privacy, duplicate URLs, and crawler call.

1. A sitemap may expose private aliases.
2. A sitemap may expose unpublished Heichel content.
3. Comments may have no stable canonical route.
4. Comment translations may be computed client-side from data not stored publicly.
5. Nested replies may form deep or cyclic structures.
6. Alias names may need escaping and fallback rules.
7. Apps may include internal/debug/admin tools.
8. Games may be static folders without registry metadata.
9. Static pages may be aliases/redirect duplicates.
10. Synchronous global enumeration may overload production.
11. Sitemaps may exceed 50,000 URLs or 50 MB.
12. Comment text may contain markup needing safe semantic rendering.
13. Search snippets may accidentally include moderation/private metadata.
14. URL casing/encoding may generate duplicate canonicals.
15. Existing client actions may expect empty SSR containers and break hydration.
16. Translation fields may need language markers (`lang`, alternate text headings).
17. Comments deleted after sitemap generation may create stale URLs.
18. Alias ownership and author display APIs may be slower than content reads.
19. Root crawl graph may orphan app/game pages even if sitemap-listed.
20. A deployment may ship sitemap code without production runtime manifest coverage.

## Improvements

- Prefer seed maps and semantic links over deep recursive enumeration.
- Create explicit public-policy adapters per content family.
- Use data catalogs already serving UI whenever possible.
- Keep comment indexing parent-scoped if stable standalone URLs do not exist.
- Give comments deterministic anchors from IDs.
- Render translations as visible semantic sibling blocks when supplied by public data.
- Batch alias lookups and avoid N+1 requests.
- Add sitemap sharding abstractions before family counts can exceed limits.
- Include explicit noindex handling for missing/deleted resources.
- Test both raw HTML and hydrated page stability.
